parsed.lead: Raids is a versus Game mode in which players attack other players' Bases to win Raid Chips and Medals.

sections.heading: System
sections.text:
Raids are unlocked at player level 7. To start a Raid, you need to spend 1 Raid Ticket, which you have up to three at a time. Each ticket takes an hour to recharge, but you can buy another ticket for 10 Energon each.

Initially, you were presented with 3 Commander you could choose to raid within one minute. Should you wish to change the selection, you had to spend another Raid Ticket. In version 3.0, this system was revamped: You are now presented one Commander according to your current amount of Medals, and selecting another base costs 2, 6, or 10 Energon, depending on the presented base's total rating.

You have 20 minutes (originally 15) to defeat the opponent Bots before time runs out or your Bots are all knocked out.

After a Bot is used for raiding, he/she cannot be placed on your Base for a period of time. Listed are cooldown times for each star rating:
* 1-Star: 5 minutes
* 2-Star: 20 minutes
* 3-Star: 2 hours
* 4- and 5-star: 4 hours
You can view your attacks and the attacks on your Base in the Raid Center. Should the raider win, you will lose about 30 Medals and 10% of your current amount of Raid Chips. Should your defense be successful, you will earn about 15-30 Medals and about 500 Raid chips.

Raid Shields can protect your base from being attacked for a period of time. But you cannot raid yourself while a shield is active, or else the shield will be removed.

sections.heading: Revenge
sections.text: When you are attacked, you have the opportunity to attack the player back, even if the attack was a failure. The same rules for raiding apply for revenge; it costs one raid ticket, and you are able to steal raid chips from the player. The opportunity to revenge expires after a period of time, usually 24 hours. But often the base attacker is unavailable to be raided.

sections.heading: Raid Events
sections.text: There are regular week-long special Raid Events when you can win Bot Chips in addition to the normal rewards. They are also accompanied with a Raid Ascent Alliance Quest. The more Medals you have, the more Chips you can earn. If you fail a raid, you will still receive half the potential amount of Bot Chips.

sections.heading: Early Raid Events
sections.text: The first raid events with Bot Chips (all-or-nothing 60-90 Chips per Raid) were available in Raids for 2-Star Bots released at the time. Each 2-Star Bot cost 1000 Chips, but Shockwave's Raid Event introduced the 3-Star version available for 10000 Chips.

sections.heading: Featured Bot Raid Events
sections.text: Starting from October, there is a Raid Event for each month's Featured Bot on the third week of the Bot's debut.

sections.heading: Throwback Week
sections.text: Running from March 8th at 10 AM to March 15th at 10 AM Pacific Time, Commanders could earn Exclusive 2-Star Bot Chips from Raids to purchase exclusive 2-Star Bots of all Bots released after launch. (586 Chips per Raid in the 1250~ Medal range) 2 to 3 Bots were available for two days in the Raid Store each day, which could be bought for 2000 Chips each, maximum 5 for each Bot. The final days of the event offered 12 x500 bundles of 2-Star Exclusive Chips for 20 Energon each, and had all 16 Bots available at once.

parsed.lead:
Raid Chips are a currency used to purchase items in the Raid Store. They are primarily earned through Raids, but they can be also earned through Away Missions and Alliance Quests.

Your Raid Chip stash, unlike other currencies, is fluid, as they can be stolen from your Base by other Commanders. A successful attack an a base gives a Commander 10% of the opponent Commander's current amount of chips. A successful base defense gives a Commander around 500-600 Raid Chips. Defeating a Base Defender also gives a small amount of Raid Chips; the higher the Bot's rating, the more chips awarded.

It is recommended to leave Raid Chips earned in Alliance Quests unclaimed as a temporary untouchable stash so you can later use them if you are a few chips short from getting a certain item.

sections.heading: Description
sections.text: Respected by Autobots and Decepticons alike and earned only through the hardships of battle, this relic is considered a warning sign to intruders that no offense will go without retaliation.

sections.heading: Relic Boosts
sections.text: *+4% Attack and Health in Raids.

sections.heading: Obtainment
sections.text: Introduced in v6.0, this high-end Relic can be bought if the Commander has 1,500 Medals and 1,000,000 Raid Chips. (Limit 1 in 7 days)

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
*This Relic is similar to the early Star Saber in exclusivity and cost.
*There are four tiers of this relic in the game files, but only the gold highest-tier one is in the game.
Category:Relics

sections.heading: Description
sections.text: Respected by Autobots and Decepticons alike and earned only through the hardships of battle, this relic is considered a warning sign to intruders that no offense will go without retaliation.

sections.heading: Relic Boosts
sections.text: *+4% Attack and Health in Raids.

sections.heading: Obtainment
sections.text: Introduced in v6.0, this high-end Relic can be bought if the Commander has 1,500 Medals and 1,000,000 Raid Chips. (Limit 1 in 7 days)
